title: Usage economics storyboard and tier messaging
content:
Purpose and problem statement:

We need a compact, repeatable story the GTM team can use to explain why usage-based (token) pricing aligns with customer value and Redwood’s product strengths, plus concrete tier and discount language that the field can use. This doc is a single-page storyboard + sales scripts + internal guardrails for negotiations.

High-level messaging pillars (external-friendly):
- Pay for what you use: Customers scale cost with value — if your app sends fewer tokens you pay less; growth follows usage.
- Predictable unit economics: Tokens map closely to compute/cost; they let developers tune latency, batching and model choices to hit business KPIs.
- Flexibility across use cases: One pricing model for chat, generation, embeddings and reranking — customers can mix and match models and still get predictable bills.
- Enterprise controls when needed: Reserved capacity and committed discounts for predictable throughput and governance at scale.

Why token pricing — short narrative for sales:
- Engineering-aligned: Tokens are a natural proxy for inference cost (compute, memory, kv-cache).
- Optimization lever: We can recommend batching, caching and quantization to reduce token spend without changing app semantics.
- Transparency: Token meters can be broken down by route/model, making chargebacks and cost attribution simple for platform teams.
- Competitive fit: Most advanced inference providers expose usage-based metrics; token pricing lets us position on better economics and observability rather than opaque seat or per-endpoint fees.

FAQ / Objections and rebuttals (sales-ready):
Q: "We prefer predictable ARPA, not variable bills."
A: "Two simple options: 1) Reserved capacity (monthly commit) with lower unit price and SLA; 2) Convert to a committed spend with predictable cadence and keep a small overage buffer. Both preserve predictability while optimizing unit cost."

Q: "Tokens are confusing for non-technical buyers."
A: "We translate tokens into easy comparisons: e.g., a short chat turn is ~150–300 tokens; embeddings per vector call are X tokens. Our pricing page and billing UI show dollars per 1k tokens and example monthly scenarios for common app patterns."

Q: "How do discounts work for large customers?"
A: "Two-pronged approach: committed spend discounts (step-down tiers) and volume-based rebates for sustained consumption. We avoid indefinite arbitrary percent-off negotiations by anchoring to clear commit bands. See discount guardrails below."

Tier design (conceptual):
Note: these are framing tiers for messaging and sales. Exact numeric prices and breakpoints are experimental — field should use as examples in early deals and run A/B tests.

- Developer (Free / Trial):
  - Up to 100k input+output tokens/mo *free* for sandbox use; limited model access; token-level metering in UI.
  - Purpose: PLG growth, onboarding, convert to paid when integrated.

- Starter ($ per-mo usage + low unit rate):
  - Example: $X per 1k tokens for generation; embeddings priced per 1k tokens or per 1k vectors (example mapping provided to sales).
  - Soft cap: 1M tokens/mo at standard rate, then progressive usage pricing.
  - Goal: single-developer teams, early product-market fit.

- Scale (volume discounts + routing controls):
  - Step-down unit pricing at defined volume bands (e.g., 1–10M, 10–50M tokens).
  - Access to dedicated models and reserved capacity options; better SLOs and priority support.
  - Includes bundle credits for embeddings or reranking depending on workload profile.

- Enterprise (committed):
  - Multi-month/annual committed spend with contractual step-downs and optional seat/feature add-ons (privacy, on-prem connectors, model-locking).
  - Custom routing policies, fallback guarantees and audit logging.

Discounting language and guardrails (for AE/AM):
- Standard discount types we permit: commit-based % off, term extension credits (longer term lowers effective unit price), and feature bundling (include Optimize consulting credits).
- Do not offer permanent unlimited % off list price — discounts must be tied to a commit band or explicit consumption forecast logged in the contract.
- Minimum deal sizes for custom SLAs: deals requiring >99.9% SLA or dedicated hardware should meet a $Xk/mo committed spend threshold.
- Overage handling: overages billed at a predictable post-commit rate; customer can request temporary throttling or auto-scale to dedicated pool with explicit approval.

Negotiation scripts (short):
- If buyer asks for higher discount: "We can structure a commit and phase in discounts at 3 volume bands — this protects your price and lets you scale without surprises. Which band reflects your forecast for the first 12 months?"
- If buyer wants price protection for model changes: "We offer price protection for committed customers for a 12-month term. Model upgrades that improve cost efficiency will be optional credits we apply, not retroactive price increases."

Competitive differentiation (how to position vs others):
- Against closed-seat/pricing vendors: emphasize per-token transparency and tooling to watch and optimize token consumption (breakdown by model and route).
- Against flat-subscription vendors: show examples where token pricing reduced cost by 30–60% for bursty workloads due to batching and cache opportunities.
- Against pure self-hosted inference stacks: highlight Redwood’s ops and fallback routing — teams avoid edge-case system outages while still optimizing unit economics.

Examples / customer scenarios (for sales enablement):
- Early-stage chatbot app (customer A): 50k chat turns/mo ~ 10M tokens — Starter->Scale transition hypothesis shows 40% drop in unit cost at 10M band if they commit to a 6-month spend.
- Recommendation/embedding-heavy product (customer B): embeddings are the dominant driver; present a vector-call to tokens mapping and offer an embedding bundle (Xk vectors included per month) with overage at a clear per-1k rate.
- Enterprise regulated customer (customer C): requires private deployment + audit logs — propose Private plan + committed capacity with a two-step discount and SLA add-on.

Billing UX & docs requirements (engineering + product asks):
- Show example conversions in billing UI (tokens -> dollars) with app-based scenarios (chat, embeddings, summarization).
- Expose per-route and per-model breakdowns, with daily trends and alerting on burn rate.
- Add a simple estimator on pricing page: input typical calls and get monthly cost estimates across different model options.

KPIs and experiments to run (GTM metrics):
- Conversion lift from trial to paid when free token cap increased from 50k -> 100k.
- ACV/ARR uplift from introducing a 3-band commit discount vs single-step discount.
- Churn correlation to metered surprises — instrument the number of unexpected overages and number of customers who converted to committed plans after receiving an overage.
- Sales enablement metric: reduction in time-to-quote when AEs use the storyboard and negotiation scripts.

Open questions / decisions for leadership:
- What is our default embed pricing unit: tokens or per-vector? (Recommend per-vector for clarity on embeddings-heavy apps.)
- Fixed thresholds for volume bands — should bands be linear or exponential? (Recommend exponential bands to align with cloud capacity curves.)
- Minimum committed spend to offer dedicated hardware and SLA — leadership to confirm $ floor.

Next steps and action items:
- Product: build pricing estimator widget and routing breakdown in billing UI (owner: Priya Shah; due: 2026-04-15).
- Finance: recommend list price/1k token numbers and initial band breakpoints for Q2 pilot (owner: Diego Morales; due: 2026-03-22).
- Sales: run two pilot deals using this storyboard and capture negotiation outcomes (owners: Evelyn Park + two AEs; start: 2026-03-10).
- Legal: prepare contract language templates for commit-based discounts and overage clauses (owner: Legal Ops; due: 2026-03-31).

Appendix: quick reference cheat sheet (one-liners for sales)
- "Pay per token, save with commitment — scale cost-effectively and keep full control of routing and models."
- "Start free with 100k tokens — upgrade to Scale when you hit sustained volume for predictable unit pricing."
- "Embeddings: we price per vector call (clear mapping to token counts in billing UI)."
- "Need predictable bills? Commit to reserved capacity and get stepped discounts and enterprise SLAs."

Document history: created 2025-11-12 by Aisha Khan; updated 2026-03-01 with finance band recommendations.
